message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Year | Key Parties Involved | Main Causes |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Eastern (Byzantine/Orthodox) vs. Western (Roman Catholic) churches | Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause), political tensions, cultural divergence, disputes over papal authority |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517 CE onward | Martin Luther & followers vs. Roman Catholic Church | Accusations of corruption (e.g., indulgences), theological disagreements (e.g., justification by faith), desire for ecclesiastical reforms |
| 3 | **East–West Schism (Second East–West Schism)** | 1965 CE (formal recognition) | Eastern Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem vs. Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Alexandria | Disputes over jurisdictional claims, historical grievances, and attempts at reconciliation |

These events reshaped the religious landscape of Europe and beyond, creating lasting divisions among Christian denominations.
